instructions: Stir the saffron into 2 tablespoons of warm water in a small bowl and let it soak while you cook.
Heat the broth in a saucepan until hot and keep it at a low simmer on the back burner.
Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a large wide pan over medium. Finely dice the onion and cook it for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft and just golden at the edges.
Add the rice and salt and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and the edges look translucent.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has been absorbed.

Add the hot broth about 1/2 cup at a time, stirring often and waiting until each addition is mostly absorbed before the next. This takes about 20 minutes. The rice is ready when it is creamy and tender with a little bite left in the center of a grain.

Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the saffron water, the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and the grated Parmesan. The risotto should be loose and flow slowly across the pan. If it looks tight, stir in a splash of hot broth.
Serve right away in warm shallow bowls. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 3 days in a covered container. Reheat in a skillet over medium low with a splash of broth or water, stirring until hot.
method_notes: Cristina's Kitchen (the lead, 5.0 from 1 rating, so a fallback lead) toasts the rice in butter and onion, adds wine, then hot stock a little at a time and stirs the saffron, butter and Parmesan in off the heat. SBS (no ratings) follows the same order. Both start with beef marrow and beef or veal stock. I swapped in vegetable broth and left out the marrow to keep it vegetarian, and scaled from 6 servings to 4. At about 40 minutes it's over the lunch target of 30, so it suits a made ahead lunch that reheats. The leftover rice cakes in the list's line aren't in any of the sources I read.
